claims.statement: sandbawks is a Kubernetes-native, E2B-API-compatible sandbox controller: an operator can helm install it on a conformant cluster, point an unmodified E2B SDK at it via E2B_API_URL, and get sandbox create / exec / pause / resume / kill working end-to-end.

evidence.locator: children: CLM-0002, CLM-0003, CLM-0004, CLM-0005, CLM-0006, CLM-0007
evidence.summary:
All six area claims are refuted, with 34 refuted leaves out of 188 claims in total. The refutations that bear directly on the root's 'unmodified E2B SDK' promise are:
- CLM-0096: envd Connect omits the StartEvent first frame, so SDK reconnect via commands.connect gets no pid.
- CLM-0081 and CLM-0077: the envd proxy and signed file URLs resolve only in default_namespace, so non-default tenants are unsupported.
- CLM-0076: /files/mint lets any authenticated team mint tokens for any sandbox.
Most other refutations are spec and doc drift.
The live end-to-end flow (helm install, SDK create/exec/pause/resume/kill) was not exercised in this audit; no cluster was used.

verdicts.rationale:
Every area child is refuted. Three code-level gaps break the root's promise of unmodified-SDK compatibility with multi-tenancy:
- CLM-0096: Connect omits the start frame.
- CLM-0077 and CLM-0081: per-sandbox routes work only in default_namespace.
- CLM-0076: cross-tenant token minting.
This verdict does not say the basic single-tenant create/exec/pause/resume/kill flow fails; that flow was not exercised live here.

claims.statement: The sandbawks-api crate serves the E2B REST/Connect API surface (sandbox lifecycle, exec, file ops, events) with TeamAPIKey authentication, tenant scoping and E2B-shaped error responses as specified.

evidence.summary:

- CLM-0081 (L4): the envd proxy is unauthenticated and default-namespace-only, and envd_proxy.rs documents this as deliberate.
- CLM-0077: signed upload/download is hard-wired to default_namespace.
- CLM-0075: the file routes skip TeamAPIKey scope checks.

Not enough info: CLM-0090 (SDK coverage in CI).

Children CLM-0075, CLM-0076, CLM-0077 and CLM-0081 show file and envd-proxy routes that skip scope, ownership or namespace checks. evidence.summary:

- CLM-0165: the S3 layout has no namespace or timestamp prefix, and the manifest is overwritten on each pause.
- CLM-0169: no --exclude-committed-zero-pages.
- CLM-0170: no RuncCriuAdapter.
- CLM-0171: no Kata-Firecracker snapshot adapter; Kata fails closed.
- CLM-0178: the capture-in-checkpoint spec's tmpfs emptyDir was replaced by a rootfs path (#656).
- CLM-0187: CI pause/resume p95 gates are 240 s / 180 s, not the spec's 8 s / 2 s.
Not enough info:
- CLM-0185, CLM-0186: clone identity reset; the spec defers this wiring.
- CLM-0188 (L4): whether the source sandbox survives a post-checkpoint pause failure.

verdicts.rationale:
Six children are refuted:
- CLM-0165: the S3 layout differs from spec §6.1.
- CLM-0169: a documented runsc flag is not passed.
- CLM-0170 and CLM-0171: the RuncCriu and Kata-Firecracker adapters are absent.
- CLM-0178: the tmpfs design is stale.
- CLM-0187: the CI perf gates are far looser than spec §13.

Caveat in code: an unreadable local binary or empty recorded digest only warns and proceeds (SkippedLocalUnreadable/SkippedEmptyManifest), so fail-closed applies when both digests are available.

verdicts.rationale: Test shows RestoreFailed on drift for legacy snapshots with a recorded digest.

claims.statement: For a capture-mode snapshot (envd_captured=true) restore skips the host envd binary comparison, so an envd upgrade on the node does not invalidate the snapshot.

evidence.summary: Passes: with envd_captured=true and a drifted host binary, staging succeeds; verify_envd_digest returns Ok early with DigestCheckOutcome::SkippedEnvdCaptured (gvisor.rs:3015-3030).

The live runsc acceptance test (checkpoint, swap host envd, restore) requires root/runsc and self-skips; it was not run in this audit, so the real gVisor behavior (code pages captured in pages.img) is unverified here.

verdicts.rationale: The gate behavior is demonstrated by test; the end-to-end gVisor property (EVD-0201) was not run, so only the node-side gate is verified.

claims.statement: pod_adapter adds a medium: Memory emptyDir volume mounted at /sandbawks/run and sets SANDBAWKS_ENVD_RELOCATE_TARGET=/sandbawks/run/envd on the envd container (cold-start and restore pods).

evidence.summary: Tests pass but assert the OPPOSITE of the spec: no emptyDir volume may exist, no mount at the relocate dir, and the env is ENVD_RELOCATE_TARGET = /var/tmp/envd/run/envd (a rootfs path under the captured overlay). pod_adapter.rs:1789-1795 documents the medium: Memory emptyDir was tried (#468) and rejected because it presents as a gofer-backed bind and trips the #237 mount gate. claims.statement: If SANDBAWKS_ENVD_RELOCATE_TARGET is set but the envd self-copy or execve fails, envd exits non-zero instead of falling back to serving from the host-mounted binary.

evidence.summary: install_from and exec errors are propagated as Err with context; there is no fallback arm that serves in place. The relocate_decision unit tests (5, pass) cover unset/at-target/relocate/marker cases, but no test drives the copy/execve failure path.
main propagates the relocate Err with `?`, returning a non-zero exit before any server work; comment at 499-501 states it fails closed rather than serving un-restorable sandbox.

verdicts.rationale: Code path propagates failure with ? and exits non-zero; no fallback arm. Failure path itself is untested.

claims.statement: After a failed pause (checkpoint succeeded but upload or validation failed) the source sandbox workload remains running and recoverable, because runsc checkpoint is invoked in a way that leaves it running.
claims.source: crates/sandbawks-node/src/reconcile.rs validation comment ('pause fails closed (source recoverable)'); crates/sandbawks-node/src/gvisor.rs pause step 3 comment

evidence.summary: The pause checkpoint command has no --leave-running flag, and the code comment says runsc checkpoint (without --leave-running) terminates the sandbox process, killing envd. That contradicts the 'source recoverable' comment at node reconcile.rs:652-657: after checkpoint success followed by upload/validation failure the sandbox process is already stopped. Whether the Pod/workload can then be recovered is not established by any test.

Tests use a stub runsc and fakes, so they cannot show whether a real sandbox survives a post-checkpoint failure. A live runsc/cluster demonstration is required and was out of scope (no sudo/runsc/cluster).

verdicts.rationale: Code suggests checkpoint terminates the sandbox, contradicting the recoverable comment, but only a live runsc run can decide it.
